policy: ALLOWLIST. A file enters the public mirror only if an `include` pattern matches it AND no `exclude` pattern does. There is no blacklist fallback: an unlisted path is excluded by default, so forgetting to exclude something cannot publish it.

named_tools.why: tools/ is 701 files of research and operational tooling and is excluded by default. Only the modules CI actually invokes are published, plus their first-party import closure. Starting from what must work, rather than from what looks safe, is what makes this an allowlist.
named_tools.closure_note: The nine modules after the CI seventeen were added because the engine itself imports them: execution/health_gate imports health_state, execution/entry_loop imports ingestion_check, execution/guardian imports collection_watchdog and (via dashboard_aggregator) watch_regime_recovery, the collectors import health_state, and notifications/monitoring import the paper and collection summarisers. Each was read before being named. Two of them needed redaction first — see `sanitize`. `daily_report`, `db_maintenance` and `run_full_sweep` were added after checking the mirror against every `python -m tools.X` line in the workflows: ops-smoke invokes all three. `replay_latest_summary` was removed — it is referenced by a workflow but does not exist in the repository at all, and that workflow already guards the call with a file test.

named_exceptions.why: Modules the blanket rules put on the internal side, individually read and found to be infrastructure rather than research. Each is required by an included module's import closure, and each was checked for rule specifications, thresholds, formulas and results before being named here.

excluded_subsystems.why: The backend aggregator imports every adapter, and nine of the fifteen adapters read internal research artifacts (shadow ledgers, S34 state, paper bucket ledgers, execution-management stop protection). One of them, `execmgmt_stopprot.py`, hardcodes a real historical worst-fill figure as a module constant. Publishing a stripped dashboard would mean deleting nine adapters and leaving an aggregator that imports nothing — placeholder functionality created to make a check pass. The dashboard is an operator surface over the private research estate; that is what it is, and the honest move is to say so.

excluded_subsystems.decision: EXCLUDED from this mirror — owner decision, publication-ready
excluded_subsystems.why: The static site is already independently reviewed and machine-checked, and it carries no numbers. It is excluded only because the target tree the owner drew does not include it. It is a self-contained artifact with its own deployment story and can be published as its own repository or Pages site, or added here by one allowlist line.

check_event_lanes states a complete pocket rule twice — a horizon and three thresholds — in a live tool. watch_regime_recovery's docstring states the same rule and imports it. Redacting a rule out of two files that exist to evaluate that rule would leave modules whose purpose had been removed; excluding them is the honest cut, and the only caller imports them lazily behind a fallback.

closure_rule.why: A test is published only if everything it imports is also published. This resolves the test suite by its subject rather than by scanning its fixtures for numbers: a test for an internal module is internal, whatever its numbers look like.
closure_rule.rule: include a tests/ file iff its transitive first-party import closure is a subset of the published set

sanitize.why: These cite internal research reports in comments and docstrings. The citation is not a leak of content, but it is a dangling reference in the public tree and it advertises the internal layout. One declared rule replaces the path with a neutral phrase; no behaviour changes.

documented_boundaries.why: Three places where the public tree reaches the edge of the private estate. In every case the existing code already handles the absence — these are the codebase's own fail-closed paths, not stubs written to make a check pass.

boundaries.behaviour: guardian imports it lazily inside a try block and calls `we_dont_have_this(...)` when it is missing
boundaries.effect: no dashboard export tick in the public tree; every other guardian duty is unaffected
host observation reports storage state as unknown rather than fabricating a healthy one — which is the module's stated fail-closed contract

boundaries.where: the research estate as a whole
boundaries.effect: the public tree is an engineering framework. The research lane that consumes it is not part of this repository, and the documentation says so rather than implying the framework is the whole system

veto_exempt.why: The public documentation that DESCRIBES this policy necessarily quotes its own vocabulary — a page explaining why preregistration matters must be allowed to write the word. Each exemption is a document written to be public, reviewed as public writing, and machine-checked by docs/maintenance/tools/check_public_docs.py.

target_note: Relative to the internal repository root. Override with --target; the path is a build destination, not a property of the published tree.

working_tree_overrides.why: Tracked files whose UNCOMMITTED working-tree content is the thing being published. Everything else tracked comes from HEAD, so an unrelated local experiment in the source repository cannot reach the public one — which is exactly how a dependency bump that broke CI got shipped on the first push.
